data_section_full_text:
3 Sample selection and data collection


I begin the sample selection process with all firms included in the S&P500 for
several reasons. First, the S&P500 includes both firms that disclose nonGAAP financial measures and firms that do not, allowing for a comparison of
theses two sub-samples through time. <sup>8</sup> Second, there is evidence in the
financial press that in 2001 the use of non-GAAP financial measures was
widespread in the S&P500 firms. <sup>9</sup> Finally, because of their size, S&P500 firms
are economically important. The composition of this index changes frequently, so I chose December 31, 2003 as the date for establishing which firms
to include in the analysis.

Table 1 provides a reconciliation between the S&P500 on December 31,
2003 and the final sample. I removed firms with global industry classification
standards (GICS) codes of 40 (financial firms) and 55 (utilities). <sup>10</sup> Financial
firms are removed because they have different regulations and routinely disclose a ‘‘cash earnings’’ number, as is indicated in Johnson and Schwartz
(2005). Utilities are removed because they are subject to more stringent
regulation than other firms. Finally, I removed firms that had mergers, spinoffs or stock splits, because this makes an analysis of the firm’s evolution
through time less reliable. <sup>11</sup> The final sample consists of 361 firms. Each
observation corresponds to a quarterly earnings announcement press release
made during a calendar quarter from 2001 to 2003, regardless of when the
fiscal quarter ended.

In order to ensure that I identify all the observations where a non-GAAP
financial measure is disclosed and that I collect the correct non-GAAP
numbers (i.e., as disclosed by firms), I hand-collect my data from press

results in a sample that only includes pro forma firms. The paper that has a sample closest to mine

Bhojraj et al. (2003) show that they are significantly better in various settings of capital market

those sources I collect the press release from the firm’s website. I use this

However, there are still 98 press releases that I could not find. Therefore, my
